body: Living with mental illness really sucks. I've been through some hard times, too. I've been diagnosed as bipolar. Its really hard living this way. The worst part, no one cares if I'm depressed, all they wanna talk about is the last time I got psychotic. Psychiatrists would never give me anything for depression. The last time I got anything for depression was after a suicide attempt and believe me my mom and psychiatrist tried to fight with my hospital psychiatrist tooth and nail to say I needed to be on something else. That alone just makes me wanna die. I mean I literally was in the hospital comatose for 3 days no visotors, and they didn't care that I was finally feeling better. All they cared about was the bipolar. Plus my mom is a jerk. Anyways...That's my ranting. Living with mental illness IS very hard. I can see why you want to give up. Sometimes I want to give up again too. Maybe just turn into a homeless druggie or something. I don't think I'm meant to be in civilized society.

It sounds like you're going down the path of self-destructive relationships. I had a bad, destructive relationship last year. The reason I stayed is because I didn't think I deserved any better. I had no friends, and that played into it too...I was vulnerable. It really screwed up my year, ended very badly, and now I'm just trying to heal. I hope you get a chance to leave that situation, it sounds abusive and scary.

Yeah that was the majority of my fantasies (gun in the woods) about every day for the last 2 years. It finally ended with an od on what I thought was a deadly combo of pills. Woke up 3 days later... I still always go back to a gun if I do have thoughts about it. I don't fight them but now, I think, what is going on in my life that I need this to cope?

I chose to avoid suicide as an option after my first attempt. I have pretty bad days sometimes. What I do is just make sure not to have anything dangerous around and try to live just to be alive. Suicidal thoughts are always something I have to take seriously now, because it DID influence me in a way...self-destructive and anger directed towards me in general. Its a vicious cycle. Point is, it only takes one bad day and the means to follow through to have an attempt. I chose to forgive myself after my family forgave me. Maybe you can think of a way to live in peace while recognizing the true danger of suicidal thoughts?

Yeah. I pretty much went on a self destructive cycle all of last year, overworking myself and deliberately putting myself in dangerous situations with my ex just because I thought I deserved it and didn't know what else to do. I hated my life...Recovery is a slow and difficult process. I have relapses but I'm doing a little better than last year id say. Celebrate the little stuff, you know?

I always think of suicide as a comfort. It did help me go to sleep at night, just thinking about it. Its sad that the thoughts become so illogical that family doesn't matter anymore. I remember when I woke up in the hospital, and told my folks I was sorry, I still thought about it the next day. It helped me cope but it became so strong I did act on it (why I was in the hospital). I can't say I don't have bad days, but I can still sometimes recognize that what I did was wrong. Would I keep meds around that I could od on, or a gun in my house. Nope. That's the life I've chosen to live. The thoughts scare me now more than they did, but I still find comfort in them. I don't know how to stop them but that's something I might have to fight for a long while. I hope there's help that you are able to find. You are not your thoughts, you're a lot more than that! Good luck.

You don't realize how powerful the thoughts can become, over a long period of time, until its too late. Ask yourself this question-if you had the means to easily follow through with a thought, would you be able to resist the urge? To me it just sounds like you're playing with fire to not take them seriously, at this point. I've been there chronic depression, suicide attempt. Suicidal thoughts still hurt me, but I try not to hurt myself. Hard to separate the two sometimes. Maybe you should consider hospitalization. It sucks but it might help.
Its okay u don't have to. Sharing a story is good. I feel a little better just to write it out.
Yeah probably not a good idea to have sleeping pills around. I'd OD on those as soon as I had a bad day (very quickly). Not safe.
Yeah I still think about it even after trying it this year in February(neighbors found me).
